parts:
Julia,

this is a matter of scale and rounding of numbers. In reality, the numbers you see when you run the lizard example seem the same, but they are not. This is easily visible if you plot them, e.g. by hist(liz.sym$unsigned.AI). For downstream analysis, variation is there, but printing the numbers in R you don´t see that in this specific example (and maybe in your own data)?

Antigoni

On Mon, Mar 21, 2022 at 9:24 PM Julia <juli...@gmail.com> wrote:
Dear all,

I have a question concerning signed and unsigned individual asymmetry index.  

I'm analyzing bilateral asymmetry using facial 3D images (object symmetry).  I've seen that within bilat.symmetry outputs there are individual asymmetry scores which I would like to use to evaluate directional (signed) and fluctuating asymmetry (unsigned). When I run bilat.symmetry function with my data, all individuals have the same Unsigned I.A. values. I've thought there must be some mistake.. and I ran the bilat.symmetry for the lizards and for the scallops data; when using the lizards data all Unsigned have the same values; but with the scallops data there are different values for each individual (what I expected).
Is this correct?  Can anybody know what could be happening? 

Thanks in advanced.

Best regards, 

Julia Ratowiecki
PhD Candidate
Universidad de Buenos Aires, Argentina.
